content: 1. The maximum dose of linezolid is 200 mg per 24 hours. 2. For third-line treatment, linezolid is administered at a dose of 10 mg/kg either orally or intravenously every 12 hours. 3. For methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), the preferred regimen is linezolid at 10 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 12 hours. 4. Long-term oral antibiotic treatment is recommended for certain conditions. 5. In adults, the first-line treatment for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) is flucloxacillin 500 mg orally twice daily. 6. The second-line treatment for MSSA is clarithromycin 250 mg orally twice daily. 7. For empyema caused by MSSA, the preferred regimens include nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours or oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. 8. Alternative regimens for empyema caused by MRSA include vancomycin 1 g intravenously every 12 hours or linezolid 600 mg orally twice daily. 9. For community-acquired pneumonia caused by MSSA, preferred regimens include nafcillin 1000–2000 mg intravenously every 4 hours, oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours, or flucloxacillin 250 mg intramuscularly or intravenously every 6 hours. 10. Alternative regimens for MSSA pneumonia include cefazolin 500 mg intravenously every 12 hours or clindamycin 150–450 mg orally every 6–8 hours. 11. For MRSA pneumonia, the preferred regimens are vancomycin 45–60 mg/kg/day intravenously every 8–12 hours (maximum dose: 2000 mg per dose) for 7–21 days or linezolid 600 mg orally or intravenously every 12 hours for 10–14 days. 12. An alternative regimen for MRSA pneumonia is trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) 1–2 double-strength tablets (800/160 mg) every 12–24 hours. 13. For olecranon or prepatellar bursitis caused by MSSA, preferred regimens include nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours, oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours, or dicloxacillin 500 mg orally four times daily. 14. For MRSA-related bursitis, the preferred regimens are vancomycin 1 g intravenously every 12 hours or linezolid 600 mg orally once daily. 15. Initial aspiration every 24 hours is recommended, and treatment should last for a minimum of 2–3 weeks. 16. For septic arthritis in adults caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours. 17. Alternative regimens for MRSA septic arthritis in adults include daptomycin 6 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours, linezolid 600 mg orally or intravenously every 12 hours, clindamycin 600 mg orally or intravenously every 8 hours, or TMP-SMX 3.5–4 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 8–12 hours. 18. For MSSA septic arthritis in adults, the preferred regimens include nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 6 hours or clindamycin 900 mg intravenously every 8 hours. 19. Alternative regimens for MSSA septic arthritis in adults include cefazolin 0.25–1 g intravenously or intramuscularly every 6–8 hours or vancomycin 500 mg intravenously every 6 hours or 1 g intravenously every 12 hours. 20. For children with septic arthritis caused by MRSA, the preferred regimens include vancomycin 15 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours, daptomycin 6–10 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours, linezolid 10 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 8 hours, or clindamycin 10–13 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 6–8 hours. 21. For prosthetic joint infections caused by MSSA, preferred regimens include nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4–6 hours or oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4–6 hours. 22. Alternative regimens for MSSA prosthetic joint infections include cefazolin 1–2 g intravenously every 8 hours, ceftriaxone 2 g intravenously every 24 hours, or clindamycin 900 mg intravenously every 8 hours (if allergic to penicillins). 23. For MRSA prosthetic joint infections, early-onset or acute hematogenous infections with a stable implant and symptoms lasting less than 3 weeks, the preferred regimen is vancomycin combined with rifampin 600 mg orally once daily or 300–450 mg orally twice daily for 2 weeks. 24. Alternative regimens for MRSA prosthetic joint infections include daptomycin 6 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours combined with rifampin or linezolid 600 mg intravenously every 8 hours combined with rifampin. 25. Follow-up therapy for MRSA prosthetic joint infections includes rifampin combined with a fluoroquinolone, TMP-SMX, a tetracycline, or clindamycin for 3–6 months for hip and knee infections, respectively. 26. For hematogenous osteomyelitis in adults (>21 years) caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is vancomycin 1 g intravenously every 12 hours (1.5 g intravenously every 12 hours if over 100 kg). 27. For hematogenous osteomyelitis in children (>4 months) to adults caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is vancomycin 40 mg intravenously every 6–8 hours. 28. For newborns (<4 months) with MRSA osteomyelitis, the preferred regimens include vancomycin combined with ceftazidime 2 g intravenously every 8 hours or vancomycin combined with cefepime 2 g intravenously every 12 hours. 29. For necrotizing fasciitis in adults, preferred regimens include nafcillin 1–2 g intravenously every 4 hours, oxacillin 1–2 g intravenously every 4 hours, cefazolin 1 g intravenously every 8 hours, vancomycin 15 mg/kg intravenously twice daily, or clindamycin 600–900 mg intravenously every 8 hours. 30. For necrotizing fasciitis in children, preferred regimens include nafcillin 50 mg/kg/dose intravenously every 6 hours, oxacillin 50 mg/kg/dose intravenously every 6 hours, cefazolin 33 mg/kg/dose intravenously every 8 hours, vancomycin 15 mg/kg/dose intravenously every 6 hours, or clindamycin 10–13 mg/kg/dose intravenously every 8 hours. 31. For staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome caused by methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), preferred regimens include cloxacillin 250–500 mg orally every 6 hours (maximum dose: 4 g/24 hours), nafcillin 4–12 g/24 hours intravenously every 4–6 hours (maximum dose: 12 g/24 hours), or cefazolin 0.5–2 g intravenously/intramuscularly every 8 hours (maximum dose: 12 g/24 hours) combined with clindamycin 150–600 mg intravenously, intramuscularly, or orally every 6–8 hours.
